title: Gemini 4 Neon
lede: Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Neon is a mid-tier model built for fast end-to-end coding, knowledge work and science tasks, priced at $3 and $15 per million input and output tokens with a 1 million-token context.

points: Google says it ranks third overall on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its xhigh level and first on that firm's Coding Agent Index.
It sits between Carbon, for the longest projects, and Hydrogen, for quick execution, and can orchestrate parallel Hydrogen subagents in Antigravity.
Four thinking levels trade intelligence against token spend; Google claims 32% lower cost per task than Carbon at the default level.
A cyber variant goes to vetted defenders through the Fairwind Program.
It is rolling out in the Gemini API, AI Studio, Antigravity, Gemini for business and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers.

points.text: Early users report a real step up in usability, describing Neon as eager, efficient and good at running tasks through to the end.
Commenters notice Neon serving far faster than Carbon on OpenRouter, about 127 versus 46 tokens per second, and wonder whether Carbon was throttled.
Whether Neon matches Opus 5.5 splits the thread: one commenter reads the Vals benchmarks as putting it just under Fable, and a reply rejects that outright.
One commenter says Opus 5.5 still feels more like talking to a coworker than Gemini does, whatever the benchmarks show.
Google's element-based model names confuse readers, who build tables to work out which model sits in which size class.
